Not Retiring—Rewiring: Designing My Next Chapter with Intention After 30 rewarding years in the pharmaceutical industry, I’ve decided not to retire — but to rewire: to reimagine, redesign, and step into a more flexible and intentional new chapter. As I begin this transition, I’m being thoughtful about how I spend my time and energy — focusing on my “Four Fs”: Faith, Family, Friends, and Flexibility. I’m looking forward to creating space for meaningful moments with my granddaughter, giving back in new ways, spending more time in my beloved Dominican Republic, and investing in the people and experiences that matter most. While I’m closing this chapter of full-time leadership, my passion for advancing medicines, supporting innovation, and developing people remains as strong as ever. I look forward to staying engaged in new ways as I explore what this next season may bring. I’m deeply grateful for the lives we’ve touched through medicines and vaccines, for the incredible teams I’ve had the privilege to work with and lead, and for the colleagues, mentors, and advocates who supported me throughout this journey. Most of all, I’m thankful for my family’s unwavering love and support. Here’s to new beginnings, new perspectives, and the freedom to design life with greater intention. #NextChapter #Leadership #Gratitude #LifeDesign #NewBeginnings

I have been with leaders from across the ViiV US business for the past week, connecting, investing our leadership and talking about what success looks like. In our world, healthcare, it is important to be clear on what success or winning means. For me, as a leader, I’m passionate about fostering a winning mindset across our team. It’s a principle that guides how we work together to fulfil our mission every day. Our winning mindset is built on three pillars: taking the lead, acting with confidence, and a cycle of try, adapt, and repeat. As Head of ViiV US, I feel a deep responsibility to ensure everyone at ViiV feels empowered to step forward, innovate, and grow. Embracing a winning mindset means staying open to feedback and change. Each challenge is an opportunity to learn and adapt, strengthening our ability to deliver for patients and communities. When we unite around this principle, success becomes collective and enduring. That’s how we achieve meaningful impact, grounded in our values and mission to leave no person living with HIV behind. #WeWontStop

When I began my career as a physician during the height of the AIDS epidemic, working for a pharmaceutical company was not part of my plan. Helping patients on a one-to-one basis was something I cherished and I enjoyed the challenge of academic research. But there came a point when I realized I could help even more patients if I could work on something with global impact. When my mentor John Pottage offered me a job in clinical development at ViiV Healthcare, I decided to take it. That was 13 years ago. When John retired I moved into the role of Head of R&D at ViiV and we have continued to be trailblazers, developing the first two-drug regimen for HIV treatment (for many years the standard of care was three drugs) and the first long-acting therapies for treatment and prevention. We have also expanded and improved the options for children living with HIV including delivery of the first single tablet regimen for children. The innovative work we’ve done on behalf of people living with HIV and those who could benefit from PrEP has been transformative. How I wish we had more options in those early “bad old days.” I’ve been doing a lot of reflecting on my career this week, because it’s my last at ViiV! I am happily announcing my retirement and filled with gratitude for the opportunities, partnerships, and achievements that have defined my tenure as an HIV physician. It’s also my pleasure to tell you about my successor, Charlotte Allerton. Charlotte is a seasoned scientist with a robust background in drug development and a passion for advancing global health, who has had a remarkable career at Pfizer. We have a pipeline of new innovative medicines and I know she’ll continue to drive our mission forward with vision and determination. While I’m stepping away from my formal role, my commitment to stirring up “good trouble” and advocating for progress remains strong. Thank you to everyone who has worked alongside me, inspired and supported me. It has been a tremendous honor to work with you. I’m optimistic about the future and eager to see the next wave of innovation and impact. Here’s to new beginnings and continued hope!

😊🤫 Although this is an individual award that recognises my work across several areas—from research and leadership to mentoring and supporting science in general—I do not forget that my accomplishments were not achieved alone. Many people who worked and interacted with me made this possible, and at times even led the very work I was involved in. Without them, I would not have achieved this, nor would I be who I am today. I also do not forget the institutions that contributed so much, providing both the culture and the conditions that allowed me to do everything from pure research to allowing me to name and organise the SCANS (Science Conferences at Noon) seminars at ITQB with a few colleagues. Thank you to ITQB NOVA for this wonderful write-up and for being such a formative part of my journey. Thank you all. ♥️

Who wouldn’t want to be part of a leading innovator in the movement to end the HIV epidemic? Today is my first day at ViiV Healthcare as SVP, Head of Europe and International, and I’m both humbled and motivated by what lies ahead. What drew me here is ViiV’s singular mission: to leave no person living with HIV behind. That deep sense of purpose is bold, but it’s also necessary if we are to end HIV. Throughout my career at GSK across some of the world’s most dynamic markets, I’ve seen how impact is created when passionate people rally around a shared goal. I’m eager to lead, learn, and contribute to ViiV’s strong momentum — advancing long-acting injectable innovation in HIV treatment and prevention to reach those who need it most, deepening partnerships with communities, payors, policymakers and more to expand access to our medicines, strengthening healthcare systems, and tackling HIV-related stigma. An HIV-free generation is only possible if we keep pushing forward — and joining a team 100% dedicated to that goal feels like the right place to begin. #ViiV #EndingHIV #WeWontStop

In the United States, approximately 1.2 million people are living with HIV, with approximately 36,000 new diagnoses each year. Despite incredible progress, nearly 13% of those living with HIV don’t yet know their status. (CDC) As I step into my new role leading ViiV Healthcare US, these facts drive home why our mission to leave no person living with HIV behind or those who could benefit from PrEP matters - now more than ever. I am deeply honored to join and lead this team, one united by passion and purpose, and committed to making a true impact in the fight against HIV. Leadership means acting with purpose. My purpose is to lead our ViiV US forward, to create meaningful impact for the communities we serve and driving progress towards our ultimate goal of ending the HIV epidemic. The Power of US is more than a slogan for the US team - it’s a reminder that it takes all of us – challenging the status quo, working together and championing innovation to deliver on our promise to the people that are counting on us. We are 100% dedicated and here until we end HIV and AIDS. #WeWontStop

25 years ago, my wife and I fully packed our Opel Corsa (half of it was the computer, the huge monitor, books, and paper files I needed to finish my PhD Thesis) and drove two days from Lisbon to Leverkusen, in Germany. The plan was simple. Staying 2-3 years to gain some professional experience (me at Bayer and my wife at the University of Cologne) and then move on. But I never stopped being challenged. R&D, Supply Chain, Project Management, Communication & Change Management, Marketing & Asset Management, Chief of Staff of the CEO, Business Development, Strategy… Leading projects and teams in Germany, France, Brazil, India, Indonesia, Thailand, The Philippines, Kenya, Côte d’Ivoire and so many other countries. Never getting tired and never getting bored. Working with so many incredible colleagues, who inspired, motivated, challenged, and criticized me. I want to thank all of you, who helped shaping the person I became, in different times of my career at Bayer. In this period, the family grew with four wonderful daughters. I want to thank my wife for inspiring me every day.
